The successive slopes of the piecewise affine roof are nonincreasing, so the roof model is convex by the constraints x₁,x₂≥0 and x₁+x₂≤r(z). Positive radii make it full-dimensional and the finite roof gives compactness. Each intermediate fiber is obtained by interpolating equal simplex coordinates u in its two adjacent lifted fibers. This proves the hull identity and the actual census at z=0,1,2,3, with no other integer fibers. An original C with the same integer fibers induces the identical mixed measure even when its continuous slices differ.

The ordinary centroid of rT is (r/3,r/3). In the heavy branch Vr₃²≥M/2 with equality permitted. In the nonheavy branch division by r₂>0 scales every planar area by r₂⁻² and gives 0<a≤b≤1≤R, 2b≥a+1, R≤2−b, and R²<a²+b²+1. Hence b≥1/2. The line through (2,1) and (3,R) takes the values 2−R≥b and 3−2R≥2b−1≥a at bases 1 and 0, as required by the touching majorant.

The ambient reduction applies to every containing closed halfspace, including a purely base-normal one. With anchor 2 and q=1/3 its margin is β(k−2)+w·X−1/3, so the four thresholds have the indicated signs. The accepted reduction compares each fiber with the original and treats a whole tied boundary fiber as whole. At bases 0 and 1 the one-dimensional clipping terms are at most (2/3)/2 and 2/3 respectively. At base 3 the term is R−1/3≥2/3, so the stated common clipping radius is exact for the given clipping formula. The scalar proof works for all β regardless of clipping. For one fixed β and common w, each actual cap is at least its separate minimum Pᵣ, so summation is in the correct direction.

For (1), 2/3−x runs from 1/2 down to 1/3, giving Q(x)=−8x²+(20/3)x−8/9. Before b/2 the coefficients of x² in the two pieces of F are −7 and −16 and their values and first derivatives agree at b/3. After b/2 F=Q−Γb² is concave. On either portion of [1/6,1/3] the minimum is at an endpoint. The three displayed evaluations follow from the envelope, and the factorizations at 1/6 and b/2 are nonnegative for the stated b ranges. At 1/3, Q=4/9 and Pᵦ≥0. The b/2 cut belongs to the interval exactly when 1/2≤b≤2/3.

For (2), r≥1≥2t throughout. On the first radius piece ∂Pᵣ/∂r=4t≥4r/3 since r≤3t, and on the second it is 2(r−t)≥4r/3 since r≥3t. The formulas agree at 3t and integration gives (2/3)(R²−1), also for r=2t at the initial endpoint and the degenerate interval R=1. The weaker coefficient Γ/2=2/9 is valid because R²−1≥0.

For β≥0 the own and last terms contribute Γ(1+R²), and 1+R²≥a²+b². For β≤−1/6 the first term is a² and the second is at least Γb², since its threshold is at most 1/6≤b/3. Adding Γ and using the strict nonheavy test gives more than the target. On the remaining interval, x=1/3+β and the fourth threshold 2/3−x are exactly in the ranges of (1) and (2). The own fiber plus the second and fourth terms contribute at least (Γ/2)(1+2b²+R²), which dominates the target by b≥a. The endpoints occur in both adjacent comparisons and no sign case is omitted.

Multiplying by V and undoing planar normalization preserves the depth fraction. Integer-base reflection z↦3−z changes j=3,2 to j=0,1. The affine fiber map has inverse because L is invertible, takes all closed ambient halfspaces to halfspaces, carries centroids to centroids, and multiplies the mixed measure and each cap mass by the common factor |det L|. A constant radius sequence satisfies both stated orientations, and each separate guarantee follows by reflection.

Applies to arbitrary planar geometry with exactly four positive-area integer fibers and implies existence of a point of depth 2M/9 for this family. Its nonheavy branch transfers sufficient tests to an unspecified point of a selected actual fiber. It does not imply the prescribed penultimate centroid.

Selects a central centroid for equal-radius reflected pairs in the planar case. A four-fiber profile that is both paired and monotone is constant, so this covers the constant boundary case but does not give the selector for unequal monotone radii.

summary: The explicit rule gives depth at least 2M/9 at the chosen actual centroid. The new nonheavy result pins down the penultimate centroid, even though a broader accepted four-fiber result already gives existence of a deep point. The proof covers every ambient normal by a fiberwise comparison and proves the resulting scalar bound for every real tilt.
